flashcard_questions.a: A distinct area of the media industry that produces and distributes a specific type of content.

flashcard_questions.q: What is convergence in the media industry?
flashcard_questions.a: Different media sectors merging together, such as a newspaper having both a print edition and a website.

flashcard_questions.q: Which traditional sector was historically the main way information reached large audiences?
Why can digital publishing distribute content more cheaply than printing?
flashcard_questions.a: It has no physical printing costs.

flashcard_questions.q: Which traditional sector is described as one of the oldest forms of mass media?

flashcard_questions.a: Any digital product that responds to user input, such as an interactive website or touchscreen kiosk.

flashcard_questions.q: Which new media sector is now one of the largest entertainment sectors globally?
What size of audience does traditional media aim at?
What is the main targeting weakness of traditional media?
flashcard_questions.a: It is hard to target a specific group of consumers.

flashcard_questions.q: What targeting advantage does new media have over traditional media?
flashcard_questions.a: It can target much more specific audiences of consumers.

flashcard_questions.q: How often can new media channels be updated?
What risk do new media products face from other internet users?
flashcard_questions.a: They can be easily copied or pirated.

notes: 12 cards: 2 term-to-definition, 3 sector-to-distinguishing-feature, 4 advantage/disadvantage, 3 causal. Sector lists were kept out of answers to avoid enumeration; each sector is identified by one distinguishing feature instead.
